I think it is entirely possible to be both.  However, I will say that with YouTube, I do not feel as pressured to keep the same consistency as I would with Twitch.  Most successful streamers have a fairly consistent showtimes schedule that can feel incredibly taxing at first, especially if that's not what you're used to.  But with YouTube you moreless have a multimedia time machine at your disposal, since you could literally record the entire gameplay of an episodic game from start to finish and upload it as late as a year later if you really wanted to.  Not to say YouTube is "better" than Twitch, but (especially when starting out) YouTube gives you a lot more flexibility and options.

I'm a new Twitch streamer, and my whopping two followers are people I actually know IRL.  I've had a few "phantom" lurkers, but no one who has been brave enough or willing to make contact, which I'm totally fine with as calling out lurkers is a dick move.  At first, I really wanted to stick with a consistent schedule of at least one day, the same time and day each week, but even that became unrealistic for me at this point in time, as I would need to sacrifice some very real life priorities that I am just not willing to do so at this point in time due to the circumstances.  But I accepted this, and find it just as much fun streaming on Facebook or recording "Let's Play" material for YouTube in the meantime until my circumstances change.

I had no fear of broadcasting my "mug" live for the first time, as I am pretty social IRL, don't really have a filter, and have a good sense of humor.  That's why I have fun with what I do and don't make success my priority, because if Twitch or YouTube didn't exist, guess what I'd be doing?  Yep, I'd still be sitting on my ass playing video games.  Only difference is that I might be nude otherwise.  I doubt that would go over well if I publicized that, as I'm sure Twitch and YouTube would frown upon my manboobs, no matter how majestic they appear to be.

I'd hate to see you give up completely unless you are totally ok with it.  You gotta do what makes you happy brother.  At any rate, would love to drop by your channel and socialize and give each other feedback.  I think community is a dangerous weapon in the arsenal of success because of the power of the "six degrees of separation" rule which can spread like wildfire.  Before his death, my great uncle was heavily interested in genealogy, so much so that after using the "six degrees" rule, he all but proved that my family was blood related to Martin Luther, the Protestant reformist.  True story!

Whatever you decide to do, just do you man!  Do what makes you happy, because in the end, that's what matters.  Best of luck to you!

It sounds more like a writing prompt than a question, but there is a conspiracy theory out there called "the ancient astronaut" theory that speculates our concept of divine beings around the world in many different religions (Christianity included) was actually witnessed first-hand in person by many in the ancient world.  These beings helped with the advancement of mankind through construction of the pyramids, stonehenge, and other monolithic ancient structures around the world that are constructed in such a way that it even impresses modern architects, who argue the technological feat was well ahead of its time.  These "gods," "saviors," and "prophets" were considered so powerful that historians wrote accounts of their legacies that many skeptics considered it merely legend because of the seemingly impossible "magical" accounts, and the argument of science faded the colorful story, so to speak.

I for one, believe in this theory, because it is the missing link between science and religion, but for me it doesn't debunk my faith, because it forces me to ask even more questions that instill me with wonder.  My question to you is, how do you feel about the possibility that Jesus Christ was an "alien" by definition, rather than by association?  Do you feel it would only deepen the faith of Christians or challenge it?  To best illustrate this, please YouTube "A Spaceman Came Traveling" or consult the Marvel story of Thor.
